chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazee' from Muhammad ibn Udhafir from 'Amr ibn Yazid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He was asked about giving Sadaqah to those who beg at the doors, or to withhold that from them and give it to one's close relatives. He said: No, rather send it to those between whom and you there is kinship, for this is greater in reward.

key_terms.یَسْأَلُ عَلَی الْأَبْوَابِ: Those who beg at the doors

ai.seo_question: Is it better to give charity to beggars or to relatives?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that while giving to beggars is virtuous, directing charity specifically to one's own kin is superior because it simultaneously fulfills the dual obligations of *Sadaqah* (charity) and *Silat al-Rahim* (maintaining family ties). This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the cumulative spiritual reward of strengthening familial bonds, a concept deeply rooted in the Prophet's teachings and the Imams' jurisprudence.
